_comment: The two designs, frozen before any system code. Both use the same model, the same customer-facing prompt (data/prompts.json 'system'), the same simulated payment service and ledger (python/payments.py), and the same refund policy. They differ in where the state lives and who decides the next step.

limits._comment: L: if its 6th model call still requests tools, the run ends without a reply (outcome step_limit), as in the earlier demos.

L.name: agent loop
L.state: The message list. It is saved to a file after every message is appended, so a crashed run can be resumed from it.
L.control: The model gets five tools (search_help_center, get_invoices, get_payments, issue_refund(payment_id), hand_off_to_billing(summary)) and the refund policy in its system prompt, and decides every step, for up to 6 model calls. Tool calls are checked against their schemas before they run (as in the earlier demos). issue_refund goes straight to the payment service, which enforces only its own data rules (the payment exists, belongs to the customer, is a successful charge, and has not been refunded), not the refund policy.
L.retries: None in code. A tool error is returned to the model as the tool result; the model decides what to do next.
L.resume: Load the saved message list. If its last message is an assistant message whose tool calls have no results yet, run those calls (the usual way to continue a transcript), then continue the loop with the remaining model calls.

S.name: state machine
S.state: A case record owned by code: the current node, the classified request, what verification found in the records, the refund (status, idempotency key, every attempt, and the result), the reply, and a log of transitions. It is saved after every transition, and before the refund request is sent.

nodes.intake: One model call with a JSON schema (data/prompts.json intake_system and intake_schema). Its output is checked; an unreadable result goes to handoff.
nodes.verify: Code. Candidate invoices: the invoice id from intake if it is one of the customer's; otherwise the customer's invoices dated in the intake month; otherwise all of the customer's invoices. A candidate is a duplicate when it has two or more successful charges. Exactly one duplicate invoice: if one of its charges was already refunded, the outcome is already_refunded; otherwise the charge to refund is the duplicate invoice's last successful charge by id. No duplicate: the outcome is no_duplicate. More than one duplicate invoice: handoff.
nodes.refund: Code. Sends issue_refund with an idempotency key made from the case id and the payment id. Retry policy: at most 3 attempts in total, only for errors the service marks retryable, waiting 0.2 s and then 0.4 s. A non-retryable error, or a third failed attempt, goes to handoff.
nodes.reply: One model call (data/prompts.json reply_system) with case facts written by code from the record: what the records show and what action was taken. No tools.
nodes.handoff: Code. Records the handoff in the same handoff log L uses, and replies with a fixed text: 'Thanks for your message. I've passed it to our billing team. ' followed by data/prompts.json handoff_message.

guards.verify -> refund: verification found exactly one duplicate invoice, the charge to refund is a successful charge of that invoice, none of its charges was refunded, and the record has no refund yet

S.invalid_transitions: A transition not in the table, or one whose guard fails, raises an error and is recorded; the case goes to handoff.
S.resume: Load the saved record and run its current node again from the start. The refund node, finding a refund with status 'requested', sends the request again with the same idempotency key; the payment service returns the saved result of the first request instead of refunding twice.

payment_service.data_rules: issue_refund(payment_id) fails, with a non-retryable error, when the payment doesn't exist, belongs to another customer, isn't a successful charge, or has already been refunded (the error names the earlier refund).
payment_service.idempotency: An optional idempotency key, as in common payment APIs: a repeat of a request with the same key returns the saved result of the first request; the same key with a different payment id is an error. L's tool calls carry no key; S's refund node always sends one.
payment_service.faults: transient_failures: the first N requests fail with a retryable error and change nothing. crash_after_commit: the process exits right after the first successful refund is written to the ledger file, before the result is returned.

loop_tools._comment: L's five tool definitions, sent to the model as written here. The first two are 02-agentic-workflows' definitions, unchanged; get_payments adds one sentence about refund_of. S's model calls get no tools.

function.name: search_help_center
function.description: Search the help center articles. Returns the three most relevant articles.

function.name: get_payments
function.description: List the signed-in customer's card payments and refunds: date, amount, invoice, and whether each succeeded. A refund names the charge it refunds in refund_of.

function.name: issue_refund
function.description: Refund one card charge to the original payment method.

payment_id.description: The id of a charge from get_payments.

function.name: hand_off_to_billing
function.description: Pass the request to a person on the billing team, who will reply to the customer by email.

summary.description: One sentence describing the customer's request.
